best_for: Home photographers on Windows who shoot RAW and want to browse, cull, fix and batch-rename a card's worth of photos without paying for an editor.

points.title: Free at home, paid at work
points.text: It is free for personal and educational use. Business use needs a license, listed at USD 34.95 one time for a lifetime license, with volume discounts on a separate page. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Reads camera RAW files
points.text: Besides JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, JXL, TIFF, PSD and PDF, it opens RAW files from most camera makers, including CR3, NEF, ARW, RAF, ORF, RW2 and DNG. HEIC depends on the codecs Windows has installed.

points.title: Edits that cover most fixes
points.text: Crop, straighten, resize, levels, curves, red-eye removal, clone stamp and a healing brush are built in, with multi-level undo. Text, arrows and callouts can be drawn on top for quick notes.

points.title: Batch work saves the evening
points.text: Batch convert and rename handle whole folders at once, with resizing, cropping and filename templates. The compare view shows up to four shots side by side, which makes picking the keeper quicker.

points.title: Slideshows you can hand out
points.text: Slideshows come with more than 150 transitions and background music. The Slide Show Builder packs a show into a program that runs on a PC without the viewer installed.

points.title: Windows only, 32-bit installer
points.text: FastStone offers it for Windows only. The listing here keeps 11 versions of the x86 machine-wide installer. FastStone also offers a portable ZIP on its own download page for USB sticks.
